description: A spray of pink spires on a rough base. Pretty enough that people forget it came out of something that was walking.
lore: It takes no edge, holds no heat and does nothing whatever, which is why the trade calls it the coming-home stone. You have been a month on the road, you smell of [[lore/the_hard_pieces|somebody else's leavings]], and you cannot make what you have been doing sound like a job — so you bring back the one thing in the bag that is only pretty.

There is a woman on the west road with thirty-one of them along a windowsill and a husband still adding to them. She counted once, and worked out that she can name every month he was away and not one thing he did in it. She keeps them out anyway. She has thought it through and decided the sill is not a reproach; it is only the shape a marriage takes when one of you goes out and comes back.
